brief: {"type":"object","brief":{"title":"Weekday Commute Campaign Concepts for Bike-Share","bullets":["Behavioral-nudge school: 'Commute Streak' rewards repeated weekday trips with personalized route prompts and small guaranteed incentives; evidence is commonly reported pilot results.","Access-integration school: 'Door-to-Door' pairs employer transit passes with docks near stations and workplaces; evidence is operator case reporting.","Social-marketing school: workplace teams, ambassadors, and rider stories normalize commuting; evidence is commonly reported campaign evaluations.","Limitation: safety, weather, and route discomfort deter conversion; discount-only campaigns often yield trials but weak weekday retention, commonly reported.","Limitation: peak rebalancing and dock scarcity break campaign promises; unreliable availability can erode trust, per operator reports.","Strongest criticism: mainstream view assumes information and incentive gaps; critics argue bike-share mainly substitutes for walking/transit, so commute campaigns may not reduce car congestion, with mixed travel-survey evidence.","Adjacent analogy: workplace wellness programs—incentives spark initial participation, but habit depends on supportive defaults such as showers, secure parking, and schedules."]}}
